- [Zero-payload checked records in Java and Kotlin, 21 October 2026](zero-payload-checked-record-jvm-20261021.md)

The [hosted Java/Kotlin zero-payload archive](../evidence/zero-payload-checked-record-jvm-20261021.md) validates the same four package routes through independently compiled JVM callers. Java emits a zero-component record and Kotlin a zero-property class. Both remain non-null nominal values; `Token` keeps its generated `Unit` member, and option presence, arrays and variant branches stay distinct.

For a record whose proofs relate its fields, use a [checked constructor over the payload fields](existing-package.md#export-a-record-with-proof-fields). The host supplies no proof. The compiler checks each input through the selected Lean constructor and erases proofs from Lean-produced results. Closed `Nat`, `Bool`, and `String` indices stay in authenticated type metadata and never become host fields; the [complete hosted value-index matrix](../evidence/checked-record-value-index-matrix-promotion-20261020.md) exercises all three closed forms at top-level copied checked-record parameters and results in all 17 consumer profiles. Top-level inputs and results have installed acceptance in C/C++, Node JavaScript/TypeScript, browser pages, React, workers, Python, Rust, Ruby, .NET, Java/Kotlin, Perl, native PHP, PHP-Wasm and WIT/WASI. npm has [installed nested acceptance](../evidence/nested-checked-record-browser-20261016/index.json), C/C++ have an [installed nested archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-native-20261016/index.json), .NET has an [installed NuGet archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-dotnet-20261016/index.json), Java/Kotlin have an [installed Maven archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-jvm-20261016/index.json), Perl has an [installed CPAN archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-perl-20261016/index.json), native PHP has an [installed Composer archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-php-20261016/index.json), Python has an [installed wheel archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-python-20261016/index.json), Ruby has an [installed gem archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-ruby-20261016/index.json), WIT/WASI has an [installed component archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-wit-20261016/index.json), PHP-Wasm has an [installed Node/Chromium archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-php-wasm-20261016/index.json), and Rust has an [installed Cargo archive](../evidence/nested-checked-record-rust-20261016/index.json). They cover direct and repeated parameters, arrays, lists, options, products, `Except`/`Result`, enclosing record fields, active variant fields and constructor-free container results. [Installed inherited checked-record acceptance](../evidence/inherited-checked-record-promotion-20261018.md) additionally covers the tested acyclic `Span → Ticket → Stamped` chain, with independently selected parent and child constructors and proof-free results. Select the record constructor and each nested checked field's constructor independently at every public input site; only an active variant branch runs. A record whose only fields are proofs is still a checked record: declare it with an explicit `: Type`, select a nullary constructor such as `def mkWitness : Option Witness`, and the host passes and receives an empty carrier that is distinct from an absent, null or default value; a record with one `Unit` field beside its proofs keeps that field. The [hosted C/C++ zero-payload archive](../evidence/zero-payload-checked-record-native-20261021.md) validates that boundary through options, arrays and active/inactive variants in ordinary and reviewed full/result-only packages. The [hosted Java/Kotlin zero-payload archive](../evidence/zero-payload-checked-record-jvm-20261021.md) validates the same boundary through nominal non-null JVM objects in all four Maven routes. Generic checked records, value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, callback, owned and open dependent combinations remain unfinished.

The selected Lean constructor checks each input and may normalize it; rejection identifies the parameter and constructor and preserves caller data. Results contain copied payload fields with proofs erased. Both ordinary and independently reviewed packages, including standalone result-only packages, passed installed checks. The tested Packet carries a Fin 10 digit and a checked Nat Subtype word as BigInteger values. Holder nests Packet, and ChoicePacket carries it in the active Choice branch. Generated Java and Kotlin adapters apply the exact Packet and nested Word constructors selected at each direct, repeated, array, list, option, tuple, result, Holder and Choice input site. Rejected calls preserve the complete caller graph and later valid calls recover. Packet arrays and options returned by Lean contain proof-free payloads without input-constructor selections. The tested Span, Ticket and Stamped inheritance chain remains a chain of nested parent subobjects rather than flattened fields. Generated adapters preserve the parent aliases and public nominal identities, erase the ordered, linked and stamped proof fields, apply the exact per-site Span, Word, Ticket and Stamped constructors in dependency order, retain independent choices for repeated parameters, check the nested Fin 8 mark, preserve rejected caller values and recover on the next valid call. Full packages check inputs and proof-free results; result-only packages project the same inherited payloads without input-constructor metadata. The tested checked-record graphs preserve nominal identity through a self-recursive Packet and a mutually recursive Envelope ↔ Step pair, including aliases, Array and Option wrappers, active variant branches, exact Nat Subtype constructors and Fin 3 fields. Generated adapters validate every selected input site in dependency order, erase proof fields, expose constructor-free copied results, preserve rejected caller graphs and recover on the next valid call. Closed Bool, String and Nat indices remain authenticated type metadata rather than host fields. The generated C/GMP, C++ multiprecision, C# BigInteger, Java BigInteger and Kotlin BigInteger records expose only proof-free payloads. Full packages validate all eight indexed inputs through the exact selected Lean constructors, preserve rejected caller values, recover on the next valid call and return all eight proof-free results.
